Definition: adverb from a compound of G5384 and G444; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:--courteously.
BiblicalUsage: Philanthropos means kindly toward men, and it appears once, at Sidon on the voyage to Rome. Julius the centurion treats Paul courteously and gives him liberty to go to his friends to refresh himself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that one centurion's courtesy is a small mercy with a large lesson: even in chains, Paul finds a friend in uniform, because God opens doors no prison can shut.
